todo_line: - [ ] 001 Record the architecture decision before further implementation.
outcome: Revise ADR 0025 into a complete, internally coherent accepted contract that closes the reviewed lifecycle, ordering, cancellation, queued-delivery, and reconciliation races before executable implementation proceeds.
scope: Revise `docs/adr/0025-use-first-class-group-memberships-and-member-owned-conversation-subscriptions.md`; adjust its existing `docs/adr/README.md` row only if needed to keep the summary accurate.

Extend first-class admission to custom-group creation: define the retry-stable creator `group_membership_id` carried by `CreateCustomGroup`, the creator-start event in its atomic creation decision, and exact retry/conflict behavior.

Define the invariant that at most one current custom-group membership exists per `{group_id, club_membership_id}`. An admission with the same current identity is event-free; a duplicate admission with a different fresh `group_membership_id` is rejected rather than creating parallel current memberships.

Define every custom-membership termination path and reason. Direct removal ends one exact membership; `RemoveClubMember` atomically ends every current custom-group membership owned by the departing club membership while preserving its existing club-removal/Admin invariants. Specify retry behavior and how the application flow correlates and awaits zero, one, or multiple Messaging revocation receipts.

Make root/reply auto-follow crash-safe: add concrete durable cancellation fact(s), bind `subscription_intent_id` to the send command and successful `MessageSent`, and define idempotent prepare/send/activate/cancel handling across failed sends, policy retries, process crashes, and aggregate restarts. Only the success fact for that exact intent may activate it.

Bind each queued private delivery to the exact group-membership and, where applicable, canonical subscription authorization that made it eligible. Define the persisted event/projection provenance and final handoff check so a removal followed by re-add cannot make old queued work eligible under a new membership or subscription.

Specify a concurrency-safe cutover protocol for both membership and historic-follow reconciliation. Name the fence/checkpoint or precedence markers, require aggregate-stream revalidation, and make canonical live admissions/removals/follows/unfollows win so stale backfill cannot overwrite a live decision.

Keep the accepted Club boundary, member-owned Messaging stream, server-resolved provenance, durable revocation receipt, system-group treatment, replay compatibility, and earlier-ADR relationships coherent with these additions; remove duplicate or contradictory prose encountered while revising.
scope_exclusions: Do not change application code, migrations, tests, feature files, acceptance tags, designs, iteration plan/todo files, or runtime behavior in this packet.
Do not implement first-class projections, reconciliations, removal commands, subscription aggregates, delivery provenance, UI, or acceptance scenarios.
Do not replace the same task with a new task identity or treat the current ADR candidate as accepted evidence.

Do not reopen stakeholder-approved business choices: empty groups remain, club membership and roles are preserved by group removal, re-add restores history but not old follows, and already-provider-accepted email cannot be recalled.
Do not use projection enumeration, projection barriers, club-wide generations, or conversation cleanup fan-out as the correctness mechanism.

references.facts: Implementation Plan steps 1-6, Acceptance Criteria, Validation Plan, and Risks require a first-class identity per admission, exact termination, member-owned subscriptions, order-independent revocation, canonical follow facts, conservative reconciliation, receipt-based completion, and exact authority through provider handoff.

The revise verdict identifies five mandatory gaps: creator/club-departure lifecycle coverage, one-current-membership uniqueness, durable send-intent cancellation/correlation, queued-delivery authorization provenance, and a concurrency-safe reconciliation precedence rule.

The candidate already chooses the Club stream keyed by `club_id`, fresh custom `group_membership_id` values, a person-owned subscription stream, server-resolved provenance, and a revocation receipt. Preserve those accepted-plan choices while making the reviewed edge contracts concrete.
Membership and Messaging remain separate contexts collaborating through public contracts; Messaging must not inspect Membership aggregates, streams, or projection storage directly.
Caller-generated typed UUIDs remain the identity convention, while ADR 0024 supersedes projection-backed club-membership duplicate prevention.
A barrier establishes selected read-model progress only; it cannot prove a later asynchronous domain transition or Messaging revocation completed.

Club already serializes club membership, roles, final-member protection, and Admin continuity. ADR 0025 may add custom-group entities there but must preserve those existing invariants and explain the partial supersession.
Source history is immutable; new canonical facts and reconciliation must remain deterministic, idempotent, restartable, and replay-safe.

Current `CreateCustomGroup` carries no creator group-membership identity even though its documented atomic result includes creator admission; the revised ADR must say where its retry-stable ID comes from and how it participates in retry matching.

Current creation emits `GroupCreated`, slug assignment, and creator `GroupMemberAdded`; current `RemoveClubMember` emits `ClubMemberRemoved` plus sorted removals for every active custom-group relation. The replacement contract must preserve these lifecycle consequences using first-class start/end identities and explicit reasons.

Accepted tests establish atomic creator admission, idempotent custom admission, and club departure ending all active custom-group relations; these are lifecycle entry points the ADR candidate omitted.

Current aggregate derives auto-follow from `MessageSent` and has no durable prepared/cancelled intent. The ADR must replace that behavior with an exact, replayable correlation protocol rather than an in-memory or best-effort callback.

The existing success fact does not identify a subscription intent. The revised contract must say that successful root/reply send facts carry the prepared `subscription_intent_id` needed by an idempotent activation handler.

Current queued-delivery facts carry recipient identity but no authorizing group membership or subscription provenance; a current-access-only recheck can wrongly treat a new admission as authority for old work.

The provider boundary currently performs a stable current-access query after projection catch-up. Preserve the final check, but require it to validate the exact persisted authorization attached when the delivery was created.

Existing restartable, paged backfill patterns are useful operational precedent, but ADR 0025 additionally needs a source cutoff and live-write precedence because it backfills into streams that continue receiving lifecycle and subscription decisions.

constraints: Keep ADR 0025 status `accepted`; the approved plan has no open business or technical decision and requires this architecture record before implementation.
Use unambiguous `club_membership_id`, `group_membership_id`, `subscription_id`, and `subscription_intent_id` language; do not overload the legacy `membership_id` term.

Name concrete commands/events/receipts or durable markers for creator admission, direct and club-departure end reasons, intent cancellation/correlation, delivery authorization, and reconciliation precedence so later packets do not choose incompatible protocols.
All admission paths must enforce at most one current membership per `{group_id, club_membership_id}` inside the Club aggregate, including a different fresh ID racing an existing current admission.

Every `CustomGroupMembershipEnded` must trigger one deterministic revocation ID and receipt. A club departure that ends multiple memberships must wait for the complete explicitly correlated receipt set; an exact retry must not create new ends or receipts.

Prepared auto-follow state must be reconstructable from canonical facts. Failed or abandoned sends cannot activate, successful sends correlate the exact intent durably, and handler retry/restart cannot create a second or stale activation.

Queued delivery eligibility must use the authorization captured at creation; current access under a newer re-addition is not a substitute for an ended captured `group_membership_id` or subscription intent.

Membership and follow reconciliation must define a stable source high-water mark plus aggregate-local precedence/revalidation. A stale reconciliation command may no-op but may never restore state superseded by a live admission, removal, follow, or unfollow.
Retain append-only compatibility for historic events and do not invent unproved historical membership periods or follow provenance.
This remains documentation-only, so do not run `dev check`.
focused_validation: Review ADR 0025 against each gap in `.delivery/latest-review.json` and report the exact added command/event/receipt or marker names plus the invariant/ordering rule that closes it.

Verify the ADR explicitly covers `CreateCustomGroup`, `RemoveClubMember`, duplicate fresh-ID admission, multiple receipt waiting, durable failed-send cancellation, exact queued-delivery provenance, and live-wins reconciliation.
Verify every relative Markdown link in the changed ADR/index resolves to an existing repository path.
completion_evidence_required: Return exact changed paths and confirm no executable, acceptance, design, iteration plan, or todo files changed.
Summarize the creator admission and club-departure contracts, including ID generation, end reasons, one-current invariant, and zero/one/many receipt completion.
Summarize the durable auto-follow correlation/cancellation state machine and how failed sends, handler retries, and aggregate restarts are resolved.
Summarize the exact queued-delivery authorization payload and why remove/re-add cannot revive old queued work.
Summarize the membership and follow reconciliation fence/precedence protocol, including how concurrent live writes win.
Report successful whitespace and relative-link validation with exit statuses.

latest_review.summary: The ADR candidate passed its documentation checks but omitted complete contracts for creator admission and club departure, duplicate-current IDs, durable send-intent cancellation, queued-delivery authorization binding, and reconciliation races.

latest_worker_result.summary: The candidate established the Club and person-owned Messaging boundaries, first-class IDs, canonical subscription facts, revocation receipt, and deterministic reconciliation outline; its reported documentation validations passed with no unresolved worker-reported items.
